ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: study
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A small reading room: a bookcase and a small one, an armchair with a side table, a light and a plant.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A quiet corner to read in, for a colony with a few books and no room yet for a library.

tips.li: Books on a bookcase don't wear out, and a bookcase near a research bench helps the research a little.
One good chair is enough for a study. Colonists read in turns, and reading counts as recreation.
A study next to the bedrooms is where night owls end up. Give it its own light.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: reading hall
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Bookcases along three walls, four armchairs in two pairs with a side table each, two lights and a plant.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A library for a colony that collects books: room for the whole shelf and for several readers at once.

tips.li: Skill books are worth keeping even after they've been read: the next colonist learns from them too.
Several readers at once need several chairs. Armchairs make the long books bearable.
Keep the hall off the main corridors. A library people walk through is not a quiet room.
A big library is a fine room to show off. Sculptures and a good floor make it impressive.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: council fire
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A round of stools facing a campfire in the middle of the room, with a gap on the side of the door.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Where a tribe sits down to talk things over. The fire warms the room, and a campfire is a place people gather.

tips.li: A campfire is a gathering spot. Parties start around it, and a council with no dining or rec room meets by the fire.
Keep the fire fed with wood. A cold council fire is a dark, empty room.
Leave the cell in front of the fire free: that's where the cook stands when the fire is used for cooking.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: council table
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A square table with six chairs, a light and a plant. Small enough for a young colony's council.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A table where the council can sit down together. It counts as a dining table too, so it earns its space.

tips.li: The council meets in the colony's biggest dining room, and a room with a table and chairs counts as one.
Six seats are enough while the colony is small. Everyone with a say comes to the meetings, seat or no seat.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: council chamber
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A long table with four chairs down each side and two armchairs at the head, two lights and two plants.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A room for the council's meetings: everyone at one table, and the chair at its head where all can see them.

tips.li: The council meets in the colony's biggest dining room. Make this room larger than the dining room and the meetings come here.
The table doubles as a dining table, so the chamber is used every day, not just on meeting nights.
An impressive room is a pleasant one to argue in. Art on the walls does more for a meeting than a bigger table.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: council hall
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two long tables set end to end, with eight chairs down each side, two at the far end and two armchairs at the head; lights in the corners.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The whole colony at one table: for a big council, for feasts, and for the evenings when everyone has something to say.

tips.li: Twenty seats make the hall the colony's biggest dining room in most bases, and the council meets in the biggest one.
A hall this size takes a lot of decorating to feel impressive. Start with the floor and the lights, then add art.
Two doors help a hall this big: one to the kitchen, one to the rest of the base.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: games corner
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A chess table with a seat on each side, a horseshoes pin, a light and a plant, in a small room.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Two kinds of fun in a room that costs next to nothing, for a colony that has nowhere to relax yet.

tips.li: Chess and horseshoes are different kinds of recreation. Colonists tire of one kind, so two is better than one.
Horseshoes are thrown from three cells away. Keep the cells between the thrower and the pin clear.
[lowtech] Horseshoes need no research at all; the chess table comes with Complex furniture.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: recreation hall
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A poker table with seats, a chess table, a billiards table with room around it, a television with two armchairs, a horseshoes pin and lights.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Every kind of fun under one roof, so a big colony never runs out of things to do in the evening.

tips.li: Poker and chess are one kind of fun, billiards and horseshoes another, television a third. Variety keeps recreation up longer.
Billiards players walk around the table. Keep the cells next to it free.
Watchers sit a few cells in front of a television, facing it. Armchairs make it comfortable as well as fun.
A rec hall is a big room to make impressive. It's used every evening, so it's worth the art.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: small gallery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two columns and a pedestal at the back, a light, and open floor for a few sculptures.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A first place to show off the colony's art, before it has enough pieces to fill a hall.

tips.li: Three or four good sculptures and a fine floor make a small room impressive.
A small gallery on the way to the dining room is seen every day, which is what art is for.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: grand gallery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A colonnade down both sides, pedestals at the far end, lights, and a broad open floor for the colony's best art.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The colony's finest room: where its masterworks stand, and where visitors see what the colony has become.

tips.li: A big room needs many pieces before it looks full. Fill it over the years, a sculpture at a time.
Columns add beauty of their own, and so does a marble floor, so even a half-empty gallery looks good.
Royal guests and traders walk through the colony. A grand gallery on their way leaves an impression.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: small greenhouse
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two hydroponics basins along the side walls, a sun lamp and a heater at the back, and a walkway between.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A little fresh food through the winter, from the first day the colony has power to spare.

tips.li: Two basins of rice won't feed a colony, but they keep a cook busy and the larder from running dry in winter.
Basins need power day and night, the sun lamp only by day. Count both before you build.
Healroot grows in a basin too, if the colony is short of medicine.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: brew cellar
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Eight fermenting barrels along the walls and a torch: more barrels for a brewery that has outgrown its own room.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Beer takes days to ferment. A cellar of barrels keeps it coming while the brewer makes the next batch of wort.

tips.li: Barrels ferment only between 7 °C and 32 °C, and the beer is ruined if the room stays below -1 °C or above 32 °C for long.
Put the cellar next to the brewery, so wort and beer travel a few steps.
Each barrel takes 25 wort and gives 25 beer about six days later.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large brewery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A brewing bench, eight fermenting barrels, a shelf for wort and finished beer, and a light.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Enough beer for a thirsty colony and some to trade: one brewer, eight barrels, and a shelf to keep it all in one room.

tips.li: Wort goes from the bench into the barrels; beer comes out days later. Keep the shelf set to both.
Barrels only ferment between 7 °C and 32 °C. A heater or a cooler keeps a big brewery working all year.
Beer is light and sells well, a good thing to send along with a caravan.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large barn
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Thirteen animal beds along three walls, a shelf for hay and kibble, a heater and two lights.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Shelter for a whole herd: the animals sleep warm and dry, and their feed is kept where they sleep.

tips.li: Restrict the herd to an area that takes in the barn and the pasture, and they'll come in to sleep.
Hay on the shelf keeps the herd fed through a winter when nothing grows outside.
Animals make a mess indoors. Keep the barn away from kitchens and bedrooms, and give it its own door.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: cold store
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A small freezer: one cooler in the back wall and three shelves. Enough for a young colony's meat and meals.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Meat and meals rot within days in the warm. One cooler and a small room keep them for months.

tips.li: [!lowtech] One cooler holds a room this size below freezing through most summers. Its hot side has to face outdoors.
[!lowtech] Small freezers are cheap to keep cold. Build a bigger one when this one fills up.
A double door (airlock) keeps the cold in when people walk in and out.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: store closet
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Three shelves and a light in a small room, with a walkway between them.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A roof over the things that would spoil in the rain: medicine, components, cloth, the good weapons.

tips.li: A small store next to the room that uses it saves the most walking: medicine by the hospital, cloth by the tailor.
Set each shelf to what it should hold. A closet that takes everything fills with rock chunks.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: kitchen with butchery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A kitchen with a stove and shelves, and behind an inner door a butchery with its own table, shelf and light. Clean floor throughout.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The butcher works a door away from the cook: the blood stays on the far side of the wall, the meat comes through.

tips.li: Butchering spreads blood. With a wall between them, the kitchen stays clean and food poisoning stays rare.
Keep the inner door closed and a cleaner on both rooms; the butchery gets dirty quickly.
Put the freezer on the butchery's side, so carcasses come in and meat goes out without crossing the kitchen.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: forge
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A fueled smithy against the back wall, a tool cabinet beside it, a shelf for steel, a torch and a stone floor.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Where a medieval colony makes its blades, plate and tools, over a fire that needs wood all day.

tips.li: The fueled smithy burns wood while it works. A stack of logs on the shelf saves the smith a walk.
A tool cabinet beside the smithy speeds up the work. Two benches can share one.
A torch by the smithy matters: work goes slower in the dark.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: armorer's workshop
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A smithy and a machining table along the back wall with a tool cabinet between them, a shelf on each side wall and two lights.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Weapons, armor and the parts for both in one room, for a colony that has to fight for what it has.

tips.li: One tool cabinet between two benches speeds up both.
Good weapons and armor come from good crafters. Keep the best one on these benches and let the others haul.
[!lowtech] The machining table also takes apart mechanoid wrecks for steel, plasteel and components.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: sewing room
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A tailoring bench with a chair at it, a light and a plant, in a small room.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The colony's clothes, made under a roof and in good light, for less than a workshop costs.

tips.li: A chair at the bench lets the tailor sit while they sew. An armchair keeps them comfortable all day.
Cloth, leather and wool are stored best on a shelf near the bench. Plan one outside the door.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: tailoring hall
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two tailoring benches with chairs at them, a light between them, and a shelf on each side wall for cloth and finished clothes.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Two tailors at once: one keeps the colony in everyday clothes while the other makes armor, parkas or finery.

tips.li: Before winter, one bench on parkas or tribalwear and the other on everything else gets everyone dressed in time.
Legendary clothes come from inspired, skilled tailors. A comfortable, beautiful room keeps them in the mood.
Set one shelf to cloth and leather, the other to finished clothes. The tailor's walk shrinks to a few steps.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: large drug lab
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two drug lab benches with chairs at them, a shelf for ingredients and a light.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Medicine and drugs in quantity: one bench on medicine for the doctors, the other on whatever sells or soothes.

tips.li: Medicine needs the Medicine production research and herbal medicine, cloth and neutroamine. Stock the shelf before you start.
Every colonist who takes drugs risks addiction. Decide the drug policies before the first batch is done.
Drugs are light and valuable: a good trade good for caravans.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: scholar's study
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A research bench with a chair at it, a bookcase, a torch and a plant: research the way a medieval colony does it.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A quiet room for the colony's thinker, with the books close at hand and the noise of the workshops far away.

tips.li: Books on the bookcase next to the bench help the research along a little.
A chair at the bench lets the scholar sit through the long hours. Make it an armchair once there's cloth to spare.
A clean floor and good light speed up research. Torches are enough before electricity.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: research wing
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Two hi-tech research benches with chairs at them, a multi-analyzer between them, two bookcases and good light.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The colony's whole research effort in one room: two researchers working side by side with the best equipment there is.

tips.li: A multi-analyzer speeds up every hi-tech research bench it is linked to. Two benches can share one.
Spacer research is slow. Two good researchers in comfortable chairs make the difference between years and seasons.
Keep the wing clean and quiet: a sterile floor, no corridor through it, and a cleaner who comes by.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: surgery
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: One hospital bed in the middle of the back wall, a vitals monitor and a small medicine shelf beside it, a shelf, a light and a clean floor.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A room for operations alone: clean, bright, and never full of the wounded from the last raid.

tips.li: Surgery goes wrong more often in a dirty room. A sterile floor and a cleaner make the biggest difference.
A bed gets the good of one vitals monitor, no more. Set the bed to "medical" once it's built, and keep it free for operations.
Good light helps the surgeon. The best doctor, glitterworld medicine and a clean room together rarely fail.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: tomb
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A single sarcophagus between two lights, in a small stone room. A grave if sarcophagi aren't researched yet.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: A resting place for one colonist the others won't forget: a leader, a founder, a friend.

tips.li: Sarcophagi need Complex furniture. Until then the tomb takes a grave, and the sarcophagus can replace it later.
Put the tomb somewhere quiet that the colony passes now and then. A tomb nobody sees is soon forgotten.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: catacomb
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Eight resting places along three walls, with lights between them and a walkway down the middle.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Room for every colonist the colony loses over the years, so none of them ends up in a field outside.

tips.li: Graves cost almost nothing, sarcophagi a fair amount of stone. Start with graves and replace them in time.
Lights and a fine floor make even a room of the dead a decent place to stand.
Raiders' bodies don't belong here. Burn them, or bury them outside.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: furnished cell
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A cell for one prisoner with a bed, a bedside table, a small table and chair to eat at, a light and a plant.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: For a prisoner the colony hopes to recruit: one who eats at a table and sleeps in a decent room comes round sooner.

tips.li: Prisoners suffer the same moods as colonists: no table, an ugly room and the cold all count.
After it's built, select the bed and set it "for prisoners", or prisoners won't be taken there.
A table and a chair spare the prisoner the "ate without a table" penalty at every meal.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: cell block
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Three cells side by side off a corridor, each with its own door, a bed and a light. Mark the beds "for prisoners" once they're built.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Several prisoners, each in a cell of their own: when one tries to break out, the others stay behind their doors.

tips.li: A prison break takes along everyone in the same room. Separate cells keep a break to one prisoner.
The corridor is the only way in. Build the outer walls of stone and keep the armory well away.
Wardens walk the corridor to every cell. Keep it short and the walk to the kitchen shorter.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: weapons locker
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: A shelf and a small shelf for weapons and armor, and a light, in a room barely bigger than a cupboard.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: The colony's few good weapons under a roof and in one place, where everyone knows to find them.

tips.li: Weapons left outside rot and rust. A locker by the gate keeps them dry and close to the fight.
Escaped prisoners make for weapons. Keep the locker far from the cells.

ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.label: arsenal
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.description: Shelves along the walls and two double rows in the middle, with walkways all round and lights in the corners.
ColonyCouncil.RoomTemplateDef.purpose: Arms and armor for a whole militia, sorted so each fighter grabs the right kit on the way out.

tips.li: Give each row its own job: rifles, melee weapons, armor, helmets. Fighters grab what they need without searching.
Build it between the barracks and the main gate. Seconds count when the raiders are already at the walls.
Shelves hold three items a cell, and nothing on them deteriorates.
